note: The full-body figure rig v3 (docs/avatar-plan.md v2 §3), measured 2026-11-09 by eye on gridded read-outs of the four approved Phase 1 figures (Gertrude r1-1, peasant woman r2-2 = female; peasant man r3-2, Kent r3-2 = male), cut by tools/art/figurecut.js. Units: the FRAME, 256 wide (one tile) x 384 tall (one and a half tiles); the tile is y 128..384, the headroom y 0..128. The figure square the game ships is 512 px at artSpan 1.5 (one tile = 341.33 px, the frame centred: frame x = (px - 85.33) * 0.75, frame y = px * 0.75). Ranges are [from, to]. The bust rig (recipes/_body.json) is the v1 head-and-shoulders rig and stays only until the bust tools retire (D10).

rules.fit: a figure is fitted hair-top-to-feet to the frame's height by figurecut.js; a hat counts in that height (Kent's top hat), so hat and head together must stay inside the headroom at generation
rules.socket: the head/body split is `headCut`, a flat row just under the jaw where the base's silhouette is narrowest (measured on the base bodies 2026-11-10: female 115.5, male 109.5; the shoulders and every outfit's cloth start below it). The face part is the base above it; an outfit (cloth + its own neck and chest skin) is everything from it down. `collar` stays as fitbody's anchor: the row an outfit's body is resampled from. It was the split until 2026-11-10 and left the base's shoulders in the head layer, showing above every outfit
rules.centre: the cut centres the figure's opaque box on x 128; the faint right turn and the near foot shift the face a few units right of centre (measured faces sit at x 128..136), which is accepted
rules.nose: `noseX` is the centre line of the FACE (the nose), measured on the base faces 2026-11-10; the faces are turned a little to the right, so it is right of the skull's middle (128). Symmetrical headwear with a centre to see (a crown, a tiara) is seated on it (tools/art/parts.js seat)
rules.flip: every figure is drawn turned a little to the viewer's right; the renderer mirrors for left (D1)

female.feetHidden: a skirt or robe hides the legs; the feet show under the hem (the foot boxes); gowns may set feet: hidden and sway instead
